sections.h2: How can a Taylor homeowner sell without a long wait?
sections.html:
Taylor owners can hire an agent, find a buyer on their own, or accept cash from a buyer who takes the house as it stands. The house itself often decides, since Downriver neighborhoods like Taylor hold many older, modestly priced homes where repair bills can exceed what owners expected.

The Census Bureau's median home value for Taylor is $152,600, and 18.4% of residents are in poverty. An owner with a mortgage and a failing roof or furnace may have little cash to spend before listing, and that is when an as-is sale gets considered.

  • Agent listing: strongest price potential when the house shows well and a financed buyer can be waited out.
  • Do it yourself: saves the commission, yet you still need a purchase agreement, title work and a recorded deed.
  • Cash sale: no repairs or open houses, with the closing date negotiated in the contract.

One Taylor rule affects every route: the city wants a certificate of occupancy whenever ownership changes, as explained below.

sections.h2: What is Taylor like, and where does it sit?
sections.html:
Taylor covers roughly 23.6 square miles of Wayne County and counted 61,279 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate. Dearborn Heights is its northern neighbor, and Allen Park and Southgate touch its eastern line. I-94 passes through the north end, I-75 clips the southeast, and Telegraph Road (US 24) serves as the main spine.

Peter Coan bought the first parcel from the federal government in 1830, and residents carved out Taylor Township in 1847, naming it for Zachary Taylor. A railroad stop built in 1876 became known as Hand Corners. Voters chose cityhood in November 1966, and the charter won approval on March 6, 1968. Southland Shopping Center arrived in 1970 at Eureka and Pardee roads, and Trader's Pointe opened in June 2018 on the old Gibraltar Trade Center site.

Heritage Park, with Coan Lake, a near replica of the old train station and the relocated 1882 West Mound church building, is a local draw. The Downriver campus of Wayne County Community College District is on Northline Road.

sections.h2: Which Census figures matter to Taylor sellers?
sections.html:
Buyer budgets drive this market. Two of every three homes have owner occupants, and the typical value trails Sterling Heights, Troy and Walker by a wide margin.

sections.h2: Does Taylor require a certificate of occupancy when a house is sold?
sections.html:
Yes. The city's building department says any change of ownership requires a certificate of occupancy before the new owner occupies the house, citing Zoning Ordinance Section 25.06. The certificate lasts as long as one owner holds the property and cannot be transferred to the next owner.

This matters when you accept a fast offer. If the buyer cannot move in until the city issues the certificate, a repair item raised in the inspection can hold up occupancy. Ask the Building Department at 734-287-6550 what an inspector will check, and whether anything on the house could fail. The department is at 23555 Goddard Road, and its building inspectors keep short office hours each weekday morning and late afternoon.

Exterior work such as fences, siding, windows, roofing and concrete needs a permit, as does interior work that changes structure. Painting, tile and carpet do not. The city says no work can start until a permit has been issued, so pull permits for any repair you make before closing.

sections.h2: What are the Taylor rental registration rules for an investor or landlord?
sections.html:
A Taylor house that is rented must be registered with the city, and it must hold a rental certificate of compliance. The rules sit in the city code, Article V, Sections 8-100 through 8-111, and the certificate is valid for three years, with a new one issued before the old one expires.

  • Fines for a rental violation are $150, then $250 for a second offense and $500 for later ones.
  • A fine can be issued for each day the violation exists.
  • Owners register through the rental property registration form kept by the Building Department.

If you are selling a tenant-occupied house, tell buyers whether the registration and compliance certificate are current. An investor who buys it will inherit the same obligations.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees come with a Taylor sale?
sections.html:
The Wayne County Register of Deeds collects transfer tax at recording unless the deed cites an exemption. The county tax is $0.55 per $500 and the state tax is $3.75 per $500 of the consideration, according to the register's recording page, and the seller or grantor is the liable party under MCL 207.523.

The recording fee rose on January 1, 2026, to $26.00 plus a $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee where it applies, a total of $30.00 per document. The register's page says this was its first increase since 1996. Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments of land contracts must be certified for taxes by the Wayne County Treasurer before recording, so a title company usually orders that certification before closing.

Exemptions listed in MCL 207.526 include a conveyance from a parent to a child or grandchild and transfers given in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure. The deed must name the exemption statute and letter.

sections.h2: When are Taylor property tax bills due, and what happens to them at sale?
sections.html:
Summer bills go out in early July and are due September 30 without penalty, and winter bills go out in early December and are due in mid-February. The treasurer checks the exact February date each year because the state sets it.

Unpaid real property taxes go to the Wayne County Treasurer on March 1, and the city's online tax record is frozen at that point. If a bill goes unpaid for two years, the property becomes subject to foreclosure for taxes. A buyer or title company needs the delinquent amount from the county, not the city, once March 1 has passed.

The city explains that bills can be prorated at closing: the summer bill covers July 1 through June 30 and the winter bill covers December 1 through November 30. Homeowners aged 62 or older with prior-year income under $40,000 may qualify for a summer deferment filed by September 30.

After a sale, the taxable value can rise, because Proposal A limits yearly growth only while ownership stays the same. Michigan Treasury confirms that a transfer of ownership uncaps taxable value in the following calendar year. The Taylor assessor's office is at 734-374-1315.

sections.h2: What does the Wayne County Register of Deeds require before it records a Taylor deed?
sections.html:
The office checks the paper itself, and it returns anything that misses a requirement. The Register of Deeds recommends working with an attorney to prepare documents because it does not provide blank deeds or legal advice, and its recording desk can be reached at (313) 224-5851.

  • Original signatures with printed names beneath them, and a notary acknowledgment on any Michigan deed that conveys real estate.
  • Paper of 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches, black ink, 10 point type or larger, and a 2.5 inch top margin on the first page.
  • The parcel number and the commonly known street address on the document.
  • A complete legal description, a return-to name and address, and the name and address of the drafter.
  • A statement of the consideration, or a citation to the county exemption in MCL 207.505 or the state exemption in MCL 207.526.

If several documents arrive with one check and any one fails, the whole group is returned. Each document should carry its own check for fees and transfer tax.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell my Taylor house?
faqs.a: The buyer does. Taylor requires a certificate of occupancy for any change of ownership, and the certificate is not transferable from the previous owner. Call the Building Department at 734-287-6550 to find out what the inspection covers.

faqs.q: How much is the Wayne County recording fee for a deed?
faqs.a: The register of deeds lists $26.00 plus a $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee where applicable, for $30.00 per document, effective January 1, 2026. Transfer tax is separate and is paid when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Taylor home sale?
faqs.a: Under MCL 207.523 the seller is liable. Wayne County prints $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, and the purchase contract can shift who actually pays.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Taylor property taxes before a sale?
faqs.a: Unpaid real property tax becomes delinquent on March 1 and moves to the Wayne County Treasurer, with added penalties. The title company will require that balance to be paid from your proceeds before the deed records.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Taylor house that has tenants?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the sale contract addresses the lease. Taylor requires rental registration and a certificate of compliance valid for three years, so give the buyer the current certificate and the lease.
